title: Publish versioned benchmark artifacts (JSON/CSV) for web ingestion with secure redaction
creator: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Context
We need a repeatable, auditable pipeline to export benchmark results from benchmark-lab into versioned, public-safe artifacts (JSON + CSV) that power:
- marketing site interactive benchmark table
- downloadable dataset attachment(s)
- reproducibility references (schema version + run manifests)

This ticket covers: (1) export format + versioning, (2) redaction/safety gates for anything public-facing, and (3) delivery mechanism so the web experience can reliably fetch/cached results.

Goals
- Produce deterministic, versioned artifacts for each published sweep (schema versioned, with metadata)
- Guarantee artifacts are safe to publish (no internal IDs, hostnames, traces, tokens, or sensitive operational details)
- Make ingestion easy for the web team (stable URLs, caching headers, small enough payloads, documented schema)
- Provide traceability back to internal run manifests for claims substantiation (kept internal; referenced via stable IDs)

Non-goals
- Building a long-running benchmark program (post-launch refresh cadence handled elsewhere)
- Adding new benchmark metrics beyond what Applied ML/PM already approved (handled in ENG-18442 / benchmark-lab PRs)

Proposed output artifacts (public)
- results.json (primary for web)
- results.csv (for download / offline analysis)
- schema.json (schema definition / version)
- changelog.md (human-readable changes between published dataset versions)
- meta.json (dataset-level metadata: dataset_version, schema_version, generated_at, prompt_set_version, regions, model list, caveats pointer, checksum)

Versioning
- dataset_version: yyyy-mm-dd (with optional patch suffix: yyyy-mm-dd.1) tied to a locked benchmark sweep
- schema_version: semver (v1.0.0 initial) so the marketing site can remain compatible
- immutability: once published, artifacts are immutable; patches publish a new dataset_version

Redaction + safety gates (must-pass before publish)
Public artifacts must not include:
- raw prompts or completion text
- request IDs, account IDs, org IDs, user IDs
- runner hostnames, internal cluster names, node IDs, IPs
- trace/span IDs, internal metrics keys, internal queue names
- exact GPU fleet SKU/instance identifiers if they reveal sensitive procurement/placement details (keep high-level class only if necessary)
- internal service endpoints / auth config

Allowed (public):
- model identifier (marketing-approved name)
- region (marketing-approved region name)
- high-level deployment mode label if published (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) only when explicitly approved
- workload config labels (context length bucket, output token bucket, concurrency bucket) as pre-defined bins
- aggregate metrics (p50/p95 latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens, latency/$) for each bin
- benchmark methodology pointer (docs URL) + caveats

Implementation plan
1) Exporter in benchmark-lab
- Add exporter step at end of validated benchmark run to emit normalized rows (one row per {model, region, workload_bucket, timestamp_window})
- Output JSON with a top-level array of rows + meta section; output CSV mirroring the row fields
- Include schema_version and dataset_version in meta
- Compute checksums (sha256) for each artifact and store in meta.json

2) Redaction
- Add a redaction pass prior to writing public artifacts (denylist fields + regex scrubbing)
- Add a CI test that fails if public artifacts contain any banned keys/regex hits (e.g., "trace_id", "span_id", UUID patterns in certain columns, "ip_", "hostname")
- Add a human review checklist step (Security + Applied ML) before tagging a dataset_version as publishable

3) Delivery & ingestion
- Upload artifacts to versioned path (example): /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/datasets/{dataset_version}/
- Maintain a "latest" pointer (server-side redirect or small JSON pointer) so marketing site can default to latest without hardcoding
- Ensure caching headers are appropriate (CDN cache for static artifacts; bust via dataset_version)
- Coordinate with benchmark results service (ENG-18566) for stable retrieval + rate limiting + fallback behavior

4) Documentation
- Document schema + examples for web team
- Document “how to cut a new dataset version” runbook (who approves, where artifacts live, how to roll back)

Acceptance criteria
- Web team can load results.json for a given dataset_version with no additional transformations
- Public artifacts pass automated redaction tests and manual security review
- Dataset has an auditable link to internal run manifests (internal-only IDs referenced in meta)
- Artifacts are immutable and have checksums; "latest" pointer can be updated safely
- Export pipeline is repeatable from a pinned commit / dockerized runner (reproducibility requirement)

Owners / reviewers
- Eng: Mei Lin (implementation), Rina Kobayashi (benchmark-lab integration)
- Applied ML: Jonas Weber / Claire Dubois (format + correctness review)
- Metric owner: Nadia Rahman (latency/$ normalization sanity)
- Security: Naomi Feldman (redaction + publish review)
- Web ingestion coordination: Felix Schneider (consumer feedback)

Notes
- Legal/comparative-claims substantiation relies on retaining internal raw logs + manifests separately; public artifacts must stay aggregate-only and non-sensitive (see data retention policy; tracked in PM-851).
acceptance_criteria: Export step produces results.json, results.csv, meta.json, schema.json for each dataset_version
schema_version is semver and included in meta + each artifact header
Artifacts are uploaded to versioned, immutable paths and include sha256 checksums in meta.json
Automated redaction gate fails the build if banned fields/patterns are present in public artifacts
Security sign-off (Naomi Feldman) recorded before updating the latest pointer
Marketing site can ingest results.json via benchmark results service without manual transforms
Rollback procedure documented (re-point latest to previous dataset_version)
test_plan: Unit tests (benchmark-lab): validate schema_version, required columns, and checksum generation. Add redaction tests that scan produced artifacts for banned keys and patterns (UUIDs in restricted fields, IP/hostname patterns, trace/span identifiers). Integration test: run a small matrix (2 models x 2 regions) through the end-to-end pipeline, upload artifacts to a staging bucket/path, and confirm benchmark results service returns expected payload and cache headers. Manual QA: Felix verifies interactive table loads in staging with filters, export works, and dataset_version switching works. Security review: Naomi validates sample artifacts contain only aggregate metrics and approved metadata before production publish.
rollout_plan: 1) Ship exporter + redaction gates behind a staging publish target. 2) Generate staging dataset_version and validate web ingestion in staging. 3) Security sign-off + Applied ML sign-off for publishable dataset. 4) Publish production dataset_version to versioned path without updating latest. 5) After marketing dry run, update latest pointer to new dataset_version during launch cutover window. 6) Keep previous dataset_version available for rollback; rollback = repoint latest and purge CDN for latest pointer only.
risks: Accidental leakage of internal identifiers/infra details via unreviewed fields in artifacts
Schema churn breaking the marketing site close to launch
Payload size too large for fast web load; may require bucketing/field pruning
Cache misconfiguration causing thundering herd on results service during launch traffic
comments: 2025-06-03 (Mei Lin): Drafted initial schema for results rows. Keeping it flat for CSV parity. Proposed fields: model, region, workload_bucket, context_len_bucket, output_len_bucket, concurrency_bucket, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_sec, cost_per_1m_tokens_usd, latency_per_dollar, n_runs, stability_flag. Added meta.json concept with dataset_version + schema_version.

2025-06-06 (Felix Schneider): Please keep region naming aligned with what marketing will show (e.g., "US-East" vs cloud-specific codes). Also need a stable way to query latest. Suggest latest.json pointer so the frontend can fetch once and then request the versioned dataset.

2025-06-10 (Naomi Feldman): Redaction requirements: no hostnames, no internal run IDs that can be correlated to fleet topology, no trace/span IDs. Aggregates only. If you need to reference internal manifests for audit, keep them as opaque IDs in meta and store the mapping internally. Add automated scanning for UUID patterns in any public field except allowed dataset_version.

2025-06-14 (Rina Kobayashi): Implemented exporter wiring in benchmark-lab branch; easiest is to generate a normalized table from validated run outputs. Pushing for JSON+CSV generation in the same step to avoid divergence.

2025-06-18 (Jonas Weber): Make sure n_runs and stability_flag are included; we need to show we ran repeats and gated variance. Also please keep prompt_set_version in meta so we can answer “what prompts were used” without exposing prompts themselves.

2025-06-21 (Mei Lin): Landed redaction pass and CI gate. Denylist includes: request_id, org_id, account_id, trace_id, span_id, hostname, ip, cluster, node_id, pod, instance_type_raw. Added regex scan for IPv4, UUIDv4, and internal domain patterns. CI fails on any hits.
2025-06-26 (Felix Schneider): Staging ingestion works. One tweak: include a short human label for workload_bucket so tooltips don’t need hardcoding. (Example: "prod_mix_v3_prefill20_decode80").

2025-07-02 (Naomi Feldman): Reviewed staging artifacts for dataset_version 2025-07-01. Looks clean. Only concern: one field was "runner_image" including internal registry path—please strip or replace with a generic "runner_version" string in meta.

2025-07-03 (Mei Lin): Removed runner_image; replaced with runner_version (git sha prefix) + docker_tag (public-safe). Updated schema.json accordingly (schema_version bump to v1.0.0 still OK; change is meta-only).

2025-07-08 (Sean Gallagher): Please ensure cache headers for versioned artifacts are long-lived and latest pointer is short-lived to avoid cache miss storms during launch. Coordinate with ENG-18610/ENG-18566.

2025-07-10 (Mei Lin): Published production dataset_version 2025-07-09 and updated latest pointer after final sign-offs (Jonas + Naomi). Marking Done. Follow-up: add payload size budget check (future hardening).
